title: Sierra and Meta Release First Draft of Personal Agent Protocol and Add 35 Partners

tickers.name: Meta Platforms, Inc. Class A Common Stock
Shopify Inc. Class A subordinate voting shares

summary:
A demo recently showcased Meta's Muse AI assistant collaborating with a mortgage agent to pre-approve a home loan, illustrating a new way for autonomous bots to engage with companies. On Oct 9, the consortium led by Sierra and Meta published the initial draft of the Personal Agent Protocol and added 35 new design partners to help refine how AI agents are recognized and authenticated by merchants. The open standard is intended to give consumers more control over their data and prevent companies from facing the technical chaos of unstandardized AI bot traffic.

The effort began Oct 6 with founding partners including Walmart, Shopify, Stripe, Genesys, Instinct, and Rocket to move away from bots that simulate human browsing by clicking web pages. A v0.1 specification due later this month will implement OAuth-based sessions and allow businesses to restrict agents to read-only access by default. The protocol provides a secure alternative for merchants at a time when major platforms like Amazon have moved to block autonomous agents from their sites.

selectedTweets.text:
On Tuesday, Sierra announced Personal Agent Protocol with Meta, Genesys, Instinct, Rocket, Shopify, Stripe, and Walmart. The response has been incredible and today we’re publishing the first draft of the protocol at https://t.co/Qao9yEfzx4 and announcing 35 new design partners.

As personal agents take on more, our goal is simple: consumers have choice and control, and companies know when they’re dealing with an agent and who it represents.

This draft is a starting point. We’d love for companies, developers, and personal agent builders to read it, give feedback, and help us build an open standard together.

selectedTweets.text:
Huge! 

Meta and Sierra just published a standard for how your personal AI agent logs in to a business. Meta, Instinct, Stripe, Shopify and Walmart signed on.

This is some of the biggest distribution platforms in agents AND e-commerce behind one protocol. 

---

Sierra (Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor) and Meta announced Personal Agent Protocol today with Genesys, Instinct, Rocket, Shopify, Stripe and Walmart. The v0.1 spec lands later this month.

Today a personal agent uses your website the way a human does. It clicks through pages, fills in forms, and phones support when it gets stuck. It's slow and it often fails.

Under Personal Agent Protocol (PAP):

- The agent reads your website to find what you offer and how to connect.
- It starts as a guest or signs in to the customer's account.
- The customer chooses read-only or write access. The session runs on OAuth.
- You choose the door: your website, your APIs (MCP, OpenAPI), or your own agent.

---

Amazon is blocking agents. 

PAP is an alternative to welcome them through the front door, albeit making them go through the security line. 

If you run an e-commerce website or online brand, your customer's agent arrives at your login page either way. PAP lets you recognize it, give it read-only by default, and route anything that moves money to your own agent.

Agentic everything feels more pragmatic by the day.
